title: [ORION-RG X2] QLDPC moonshot — discover decoder obstruction/normal-form theory and certified accuracy-latency phases
body:
Parent: #894.
Scientific role: highest-value physical/scientific transfer of ORION-RG.

## Mission

Do not build another decoder benchmark. Determine whether modern QLDPC decoder improvements can be explained and extended by a common structural theory:

`decoder failure obstruction -> semantics-preserving graph/state transformation -> restored inference/convergence -> certified accuracy/latency/resource regime`.

Strongest target: discover a reusable transformation/normal-form theorem that predicts or constructs a decoder mechanism from code/noise/hardware structure, then confirm it prospectively against strong current decoders.

## Current donor frontier to absorb

The 2026 baseline is already strong and must receive first refusal:

- BP+Ordered Tanner Forest (OTF): almost-linear post-processing; removes qubits/edges until a tree-like condition enables guaranteed BP convergence under its stated support condition; circuit-level sparsification uses a transfer map for soft information.
- GARI: graph augmentation/rewiring for correlated QLDPC errors; preserves decoding equivalence while eliminating harmful short-cycle/correlation structure; a 2026 FPGA implementation reports 596 ns average decoding latency on the [[144,12,12]] BB-code case study.
- BP-guided Beam Search: tunable speed/accuracy frontier; PRX Quantum 2026 reports strong logical-error and tail-latency improvements over BP-OSD for selected beam widths.
- BP-OSD and other current QLDPC decoders remain mandatory comparators where applicable.

No novelty credit for BP, OSD, OTF, GARI, beam search, FPGA acceleration, Tanner-graph cycle removal, detector-error-model sparsification, or generic decoder selection.

## Expert council

- QEC/code theorist — syndrome/logical correctness and code-family scope;
- graphical-inference theorist — BP fixed points, trapping sets, loops, correlations, factor-graph transformations;
- algorithm/complexity lead — runtime/tail-latency and exact vs heuristic state;
- hardware/QEC-systems lead — FPGA/CPU/ASIC and QEC-round budgets;
- ORION-RG structural lead — obstruction quotient, normal-form transformations, phase cells;
- hostile decoder reviewer — compare every mechanism to strongest current donor and reject hidden-code/noise advantages.

## X2-A — common obstruction language

On prospectively frozen code/noise families, define exact decoder-obstruction coordinates before comparing outcomes. Candidate coordinates include:

- short-cycle/correlation motifs in detector/factor graphs;
- BP residual/nonconvergence signatures;
- local rank/degeneracy and syndrome-support structure;
- reliability concentration / ambiguity measures;
- trapping-set-like subgraphs where mathematically applicable;
- sparsification/rewiring sensitivity;
- posterior-entropy or competing-candidate structure;
- graph expansion/tree-likeness measures;
- hardware-relevant parallelism/memory locality.

The language is frozen before protected regime labels are opened. Feature usefulness alone is not a theorem.

## X2-B — mechanism correspondence test

For each donor decoder/transformation, reconstruct a proof-carrying map:

`obstruction signature -> action -> semantic equivalence/correctness -> resource delta -> observed/guaranteed effect`.

Ask whether OTF, GARI and beam-search escalation are instances of a smaller set of primitive obstruction-removal operations, or whether they require fundamentally different state.

Strong positive:

`X2_COMMON_DECODER_OBSTRUCTION_BASIS_SUPPORTED`

Honest negative:

`X2_DONOR_MECHANISMS_REQUIRE_INCOMPATIBLE_STATE__NO_COMMON_BASIS`

## X2-C — exact small-world state quotient

Construct exact/sufficient small QLDPC or detector-graph worlds where the full decoder outcome can be exhaustively checked. Compute continuation/value/regime equivalence classes analogous to RG/QG state quotients.

Questions:
- how much state is needed to decide `BP_SUFFICIENT / REWIRE / FORESTIFY / SEARCH_ESCALATE / CANNOT_CHECK`?
- is regime-label state substantially smaller than exact maximum-likelihood/error-vector state?
- which omitted coordinate creates the first mixed cell?

A bounded quotient is not an all-code theorem, but it guides the structural theorem search.

## X2-D — new transformation theorem search

Counterexample-first. Freeze a bounded grammar of graph/inference transformations not identical to a donor method but constructed from donor-valid primitives, for example:

- correlation-preserving cycle surgery;
- reliability-conditioned local forestification;
- decomposition into weakly coupled inference components with exact interface messages;
- adaptive augmentation/rewiring chosen from a finite obstruction basis;
- bounded candidate branching only on provably ambiguous quotient classes.

A candidate must preserve the exact decoding problem or carry an explicit approximation/error bound. It must not obtain a stronger noise oracle or hidden gold error.

Strong theorem target:

> Under an explicit graph/noise structural condition C, transformation T preserves the decoding problem and moves every admitted obstruction into a class where inference method M converges/succeeds, with a proved complexity/resource bound.

## X2-E — certified regime geometry

For frozen code/noise/hardware parameters `x`, define a decoder resource vector rather than one scalar:

`(logical_error, avg_latency, tail_latency, memory, parallelism, area/power proxy, preprocessing, update cost)`.

Seek certified/empirically prospectively validated cells where one mechanism is preferred subject to hard accuracy/latency constraints.

The scientific prediction is made before opening the full held-out decoder panel:

`structure + p + hardware budget -> decoder mechanism/parameter regime`.

Outside a certified cell returns `CANNOT_CHECK`, not a forced choice.

## X2-F — held-out confirmation

After all structural rules and phase boundaries are frozen, test on at least:

- a held-out BB-code size/parameter point;
- one materially different QLDPC code family if reproducible circuit-level models are available;
- a changed noise-correlation regime;
- a changed hardware latency/resource budget.

Strongest current donor receives the same detector/noise information and preprocessing budget.

## Strong terminals

- `X2_NEW_QLDPC_DECODER_TRANSFORMATION_THEOREM_PROVED`
- `X2_COMMON_DECODER_OBSTRUCTION_BASIS_SUPPORTED`
- `X2_REGIME_RECOGNITION_STATE_STRICTLY_SMALLER_THAN_EXACT_DECODING_STATE`
- `X2_PROSPECTIVE_ACCURACY_LATENCY_REGIME_FORECAST_CONFIRMED`
- `X2_NEW_DECODER_PARETO_REGIME_BEATS_FROZEN_DONOR_FRONTIER`
- `X2_DONOR_COMPOSITION_SUFFICIENT`
- `X2_NO_COMMON_STRUCTURAL_STATE`
- `X2_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Claim boundary

Simulation/benchmark success alone is not a new decoding theorem. Hardware projections are not real-QPU advantage. Any new decoder claim must survive exact syndrome/logical verification, matched information, strong donor comparison and independent replay.
